source: Australian Government and International Union for Conservation of Nature — Blue Carbon Accelerator Fund
status_note: Selected under the first BCAF readiness call in 2022; the Australia-IUCN BCAF partnership ended in 2025.

document_title: BCAF Readiness I — ZSL and Coast4C Mangrove Blue Carbon Feasibility Project
notes: The Blue Carbon Accelerator Fund supported the Zoological Society of London and Coast4C in preparing a large-scale mangrove protection and restoration project. Readiness activities included mapping, carbon modelling, commercial assessment, livelihood analysis and a detailed feasibility assessment of financial viability. The project prepared a pathway toward certification and investment, but it did not itself certify credits, authorize restoration activities nationally or provide a completed independently verified removal result.
source: Australian Government and International Union for Conservation of Nature — Blue Carbon Accelerator Fund
status_note: Selected under the first BCAF readiness call in 2022; the Australia-IUCN BCAF partnership ended in 2025.

document_title: BCAF Readiness II — Forest Carbon Mangrove and Seagrass Market Readiness Project
notes: The Blue Carbon Accelerator Fund supported Forest Carbon and a local community protecting coastal ecosystems within a 42,000-hectare marine protected area. The project assessed biodiversity and developed a monitoring programme covering mangrove and seagrass carbon sequestration to inform certification and international market engagement. It was a readiness and evidence-building project and did not itself issue credits, establish an Indonesian methodology or authorize a new restoration project.
source: Australian Government and International Union for Conservation of Nature — Blue Carbon Accelerator Fund
status_note: Selected through the latest BCAF readiness call announced in January 2024; the Australia-IUCN BCAF partnership ended in 2025.

document_title: BCAF Readiness II — EcoSecurities Blue Carbon Investment Readiness Project
notes: The Blue Carbon Accelerator Fund supported EcoSecurities in preparing restoration and conservation of a Malaysian blue carbon ecosystem for private investment. The feasibility study included a carbon model, landscape analysis, legal and institutional rights assessment and technical and socio-economic field surveys, producing a management profile and investment roadmap. The project did not itself certify carbon credits, establish a national accounting method or verify completed carbon removals.
source: Australian Government and International Union for Conservation of Nature — Blue Carbon Accelerator Fund
status_note: Selected through the latest BCAF readiness call announced in January 2024; the Australia-IUCN BCAF partnership ended in 2025.

document_title: BCAF Readiness II — Rare Community Blue Carbon Market Pre-Feasibility Project
notes: The Blue Carbon Accelerator Fund supported Rare in assessing options to restore and manage a Philippine blue carbon ecosystem through community empowerment. The project combined stakeholder assessment with a market pre-feasibility study covering regulation, carbon sequestration, market potential, financing pathways and biodiversity-friendly enterprises. It supported project design and capacity building but did not create a crediting programme, issue credits or verify a completed net-removal outcome.
source: Australian Government and International Union for Conservation of Nature — Blue Carbon Accelerator Fund
status_note: Selected through the latest BCAF readiness call announced in January 2024; the Australia-IUCN BCAF partnership ended in 2025.

document_title: BCAF Readiness II — RePLANET Mangrove Restoration under Forest Carbon Laws
notes: The Blue Carbon Accelerator Fund supported RePLANET in developing a mangrove restoration project under Indonesia's forest-carbon legal framework. The proposed project aimed to restore up to 2,000 hectares of abandoned or underused shrimp farms, allocate 60 percent of revenue to local stakeholders and attract private investment. The readiness funding helped navigate legal requirements and prepare the project; it did not establish that the full area was restored, that credits were issued or that a final removal quantity was verified.
source: Australian Government and International Union for Conservation of Nature — Blue Carbon Accelerator Fund
status_note: Selected through the latest BCAF readiness call announced in January 2024; the Australia-IUCN BCAF partnership ended in 2025.

document_title: Roberts Bay Blue Carbon Project — Federal Contribution Agreement
notes: Environment and Climate Change Canada disclosed a CAD 250,000 multi-year contribution to Peninsula Streams Society for the Roberts Bay Blue Carbon Project. Recipient materials linked the award to baseline assessment and the proposed Mermaid Creek salt-marsh restoration intended to enhance blue carbon sequestration and coastal resilience. The restoration component was cancelled in 2024 because unresolved riparian property-rights issues prevented implementation within the funding timeline. The contribution therefore did not produce the planned restoration, verified removals or carbon credits.
source: Environment and Climate Change Canada
status_note: The federal contribution was disclosed in 2022; the recipient reported cancellation of the restoration project in February 2024.

document_title: Accelerated Discovery of Metal-Organic Frameworks for Ocean Carbon Capture
notes: The National Research Council Canada provided a CAD 154,000 grant for an AI- and laboratory-automation framework to discover and optimize metal-organic frameworks for carbon capture and utilization. The project specifically included bicarbonate capture from ocean-related streams and electrochemical carbon-dioxide conversion while considering stability, synthesizability, toxicity and industry standards. The award supported materials discovery and dataset development; it did not authorize direct ocean capture deployment, certify a capture process or verify carbon removals.
source: National Research Council Canada
status_note: Agreement period: 1 May 2024 to 31 March 2026.

document_title: IMFN Climate FY2025/26 — CAROOD Mangrove Restoration Project
notes: Natural Resources Canada provided a CAD 125,000 contribution to the CAROOD Watershed Model Forest Management Council to scale forest and mangrove restoration, inclusive landscape governance and sustainable livelihoods in the Philippines. The project also supported education and outreach for youth, women and local organisations. The contribution funded restoration and capacity building but did not state a quantified additional marine carbon-removal result, a blue-carbon accounting methodology or issued credits.
source: Natural Resources Canada — Global Forest Leadership Program
status_note: Agreement period: 10 September 2025 to 31 March 2026.

document_title: Ka Tikina Ake Ai He Wai Hei Oranga Mo Te Ao Katoa — Ahipara Reef Blue Carbon Project
notes: New Zealand's Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment awarded NZD 250,000 to Te Runanga o Te Rarawa Trustee Limited for a one-year Māori-led project in the Ahipara Takiwā. The project mapped reef species and habitat, estimated carbon value and used machine learning, three-dimensional mapping, drones and environmental DNA to support reef restoration and possible blue-carbon investment. The grant funded research and capability building; it did not create a national crediting methodology, issue credits or verify a completed carbon-removal quantity.
source: New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment
status_note: Awarded under the 2023 He aka ka toro Navigation Fund for a one-year project beginning in the 2024 implementation window.

document_title: Te Heriheri Wetland — Waihī Estuary Restoration and Blue Carbon Research
notes: Bay of Plenty Regional Council and Te Wahapū o Waihī developed Te Heriheri Wetland, formerly the Cutwater Road Wetland, by converting low-lying farmland beside Waihī Estuary back to coastal wetland. The project supports water-quality improvement, indigenous habitat, biodiversity and carbon storage, and hosted blue-carbon research by The Nature Conservancy Aotearoa in 2024. Construction and water-flow restoration have proceeded, but the public record does not provide a verified additional carbon-removal quantity, an approved crediting methodology or issued carbon credits.
source: Bay of Plenty Regional Council and Te Wahapū o Waihī
status_note: The joint venture was announced in June 2023; earthworks and wetland re-establishment continued through 2024–2026.

document_title: An Alkaline Solution to Acidification and Carbon Uptake in New Zealand Waters
notes: New Zealand's Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment awarded NZD 1 million for a two-year Smart Ideas project examining an alkaline approach to ocean acidification and carbon uptake in New Zealand waters, followed by a NZD 500,000 extension. The award supports scientific and technological research into alkalinity-based carbon uptake. It does not itself authorize ocean dosing, establish a national MRV methodology, certify carbon credits or demonstrate verified removal at scale.
source: New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment — Endeavour Fund
status_note: Initial contract: 1 October 2024 to 30 September 2026; extension: 1 October 2026 to 30 September 2027.

document_title: Carbon Footprints Underwater — Seabed Carbon Disturbance Assessment Project
notes: New Zealand's Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment funded a University of Auckland project to develop methods for assessing carbon dioxide released when seafloor sediments are disturbed and resuspended. The project developed carbon-footprint assessment methods and an extension is building an application linked to fishing-activity data to support management decisions. It is an evidence and monitoring project and does not constitute carbon removal, a mandatory fisheries rule or a certified blue-carbon accounting methodology.
source: New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment — Endeavour Fund
status_note: Initial contract: 1 October 2023 to 30 September 2026; extension: 1 October 2026 to 30 September 2027.

document_title: Scottish Blue Carbon Action Plan — Islands Communities Impact Assessment
notes: The Scottish Government completed an Islands Communities Impact Assessment for the Scottish Blue Carbon Action Plan. The assessment considered how evidence-building and future policy integration concerning saltmarsh, seagrass, seabed sediments, kelp and seaweed could affect island communities and stakeholders. It is a supporting social and policy assessment and does not create a restoration programme, authorize marine activities, establish a carbon-credit method or quantify additional removals.
source: Scottish Government — Marine Directorate
status_note: Published on 8 December 2025 as a completed impact assessment supporting the Scottish Blue Carbon Action Plan.

document_title: Orkney Islands Regional Marine Plan
notes: The statutory regional marine plan directs marine planning and decision-making in Orkney. It identifies safeguarding and, where appropriate, restoring blue carbon habitats as a climate-adaptation measure, recognises carbon sequestration and storage as ecosystem services, and requires development proposals to address climate mitigation, adaptation and nature-based resilience. The plan influences authorization decisions but does not itself approve a restoration project, establish a carbon-credit methodology or quantify additional removals.
source: Scottish Government and Orkney Marine Planning Advisory Group
status_note: Published and adopted in February 2026 as the regional marine plan for the Orkney Islands marine region.

document_title: Coccolithophore Controls on Ocean Alkalinity (CHALKY)
notes: The Natural Environment Research Council funded a multi-institution research programme examining how coccolithophores and carbonate production control ocean alkalinity. The programme supports observations, experiments and modelling of calcification and carbonate chemistry across several United Kingdom research institutions. It is fundamental carbon-cycle research and does not authorize ocean alkalinity enhancement, establish an MRV standard or verify engineered removals.
source: Natural Environment Research Council — UK Research and Innovation
status_note: The linked institutional awards began in November 2023 and run through 2026–2027.

document_title: Fish Gut Carbonates and the Control of Ocean Alkalinity
notes: The Natural Environment Research Council funded research on fish-produced carbonates and their influence on ocean alkalinity. The project examined a biological source of marine carbonate and its significance for ocean carbon chemistry and alkalinity budgets. It was fundamental research completed in 2024 and did not constitute an alkalinity-enhancement engineering project, a monitoring standard or a carbon-credit methodology.
source: Natural Environment Research Council — UK Research and Innovation
status_note: Award period: August 2022 to September 2024.

document_title: MaSCOt — Marine Sensors for Carbon Observations
notes: The Natural Environment Research Council funded the MaSCOt project to advance marine sensors and observational capability for ocean carbon measurements. The project supports development and application of instruments needed to improve carbon-cycle observations and data quality. It is an active research-infrastructure award and does not establish a statutory MRV requirement, certify carbon-removal credits or authorize a marine CDR deployment.
source: Natural Environment Research Council — UK Research and Innovation
status_note: Lead award period: November 2024 to March 2027.

document_title: PARTITRICS — Particle Transformation and Respiration Influence on Ocean Carbon Storage
notes: The Natural Environment Research Council funded PARTITRICS to investigate how particle transformation and respiration affect ocean carbon storage. The multi-institution programme examines processes controlling the fate of sinking organic particles and the efficiency of biological carbon export. It is active fundamental research and does not create a negative-emissions project, deployment authorization or carbon-credit methodology.
source: Natural Environment Research Council — UK Research and Innovation
status_note: The lead award began in November 2023 and runs to October 2026.

document_title: CarTRidge — Enhanced Carbon Export Driven by Internal Tides over the Mid-Atlantic Ridge
notes: The Natural Environment Research Council funded CarTRidge to investigate enhanced biological carbon export associated with internal tides over the Mid-Atlantic Ridge. The project combines ocean observations and process research to clarify physical controls on carbon transport and storage. It is an active scientific study and does not constitute artificial upwelling, engineered carbon removal, a crediting method or deployment authorization.
source: Natural Environment Research Council — UK Research and Innovation
status_note: Linked institutional awards began in August–September 2024 and run through January–February 2027.

document_title: Impacts of Bottom Trawling on Seabed Carbon Storage
notes: The Natural Environment Research Council funded a major research programme on how bottom trawling affects seabed carbon storage. The project supports field, analytical and modelling work intended to quantify disturbance effects and improve evidence for marine management. It is an active research award and does not itself impose fishing restrictions, establish a carbon-credit method or claim engineered carbon removal.
source: Natural Environment Research Council — UK Research and Innovation
status_note: Lead award period: January 2025 to December 2028.

document_title: MicroRESPIRE — Microbial Respiration as a Key Process in Ocean Carbon Storage
notes: The Natural Environment Research Council funded MicroRESPIRE to examine the abiotic and biotic factors controlling microbial respiration, a key process affecting ocean carbon storage. The research improved understanding of how microbial activity changes the persistence and fate of organic carbon. It was completed in 2026 and did not establish a microbial negative-emissions technology, deployment programme, MRV standard or carbon credits.
source: Natural Environment Research Council — UK Research and Innovation
status_note: Award period: August 2022 to March 2026.

document_title: Strengthening Climate Resilience, Saving Endangered Species and Improving Livelihoods in Belize
notes: Global Affairs Canada provided CAD 48,812 to the Clearwater Marine Aquarium Research Institute Belize for a coastal resilience project in Gales Point Village. The project expanded seagrass monitoring and mangrove restoration, supported local climate education, collected information on endangered manatees and linked regenerative land activities with carbon sequestration and livelihoods. The contribution supported restoration, monitoring and community capacity building, but it did not establish a blue-carbon crediting method, issue credits or report a verified quantity of additional marine carbon removal.
source: Global Affairs Canada — International Development Assistance Program
status_note: Agreement period: 13 December 2024 to 31 March 2026.

document_title: CarbOcean — An Integrative Approach to Unravel the Ocean's Biological Carbon Pump
notes: The European Research Council funded CarbOcean to develop a mechanistic and quantitative understanding of the biological carbon pump. The project combines autonomous robotic profilers, simultaneous observations of particulate organic and inorganic carbon, biogeochemical modelling, remote sensing and artificial intelligence to examine carbon export from the surface ocean to the twilight zone and deep ocean. It is an active scientific and observational programme and does not authorize engineered ocean carbon removal, establish a crediting methodology or verify project-level removals.
source: European Commission — CORDIS / European Research Council
status_note: Project period: 1 May 2021 to 30 April 2028.

document_title: CAPTURE — Carbon Pathways in the Southern Ocean
notes: The European Union funded CAPTURE to quantify biological-carbon-pump pathways in the Southern Ocean using year-round, depth-resolved observations from biogeochemical Argo floats. The research examined sinking particles, vertical mixing and active transport by vertically migrating organisms to improve ocean carbon budgets and understanding of deep-ocean carbon export. The project was completed as scientific research and did not create an ocean-fertilization programme, authorize material addition or issue carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS / Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2021 to 31 January 2024.

document_title: SO-CUP — Southern Ocean Carbon Uptake
notes: The European Union funded SO-CUP to identify and quantify the processes controlling inorganic-carbon uptake and storage through Subantarctic Mode Water and Antarctic Intermediate Water. The project combined biogeochemical Argo observations with a high-resolution data-assimilating ocean model to improve prediction of Southern Ocean carbon uptake under climate change. It was completed as a research project and did not establish an engineered carbon-removal activity, an MRV standard or a carbon-credit programme.
source: European Commission — CORDIS / Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions
status_note: Project period: 1 September 2020 to 31 October 2022.

document_title: MINORG — The Role of Minerals in the Oceanic Carbon Cycle
notes: The European Research Council funded MINORG to investigate how minerals interact with organic matter and influence the transport, transformation and preservation of carbon in the ocean. The project addressed poorly constrained mechanisms connecting mineral particles with carbon export and long-term storage. It was completed as fundamental research and did not involve deliberate mineral addition for ocean alkalinity enhancement, commercial deployment, permitting or carbon-credit issuance.
source: European Commission — CORDIS / European Research Council
status_note: Project period: 1 June 2017 to 31 August 2023.

document_title: Symbio-CB-Seagrass — Symbiotic Interaction with Cable Bacteria for Seagrass Health
notes: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie project investigates interactions between seagrasses and cable bacteria and how microbial sulphur cycling may support seagrass health and resilience. Because seagrass meadows are blue-carbon ecosystems, the work contributes to understanding the biological and biogeochemical processes that sustain carbon-storing coastal habitats. The project is active research and does not constitute a seagrass-restoration programme, quantify additional removals or establish carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS / Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2027.

document_title: GOCART — Gauging Ocean Organic Carbon Fluxes Using Autonomous Robotic Technologies
notes: The European Research Council funded GOCART to use autonomous underwater vehicles and high-frequency observations to determine how sinking organic matter is remineralised and how the depth of remineralisation controls ocean carbon storage. The project advanced observational technology and understanding of the biological carbon pump. It was completed as research and did not authorize ocean engineering, establish an official MRV methodology or verify commercial carbon removals.
source: European Commission — CORDIS / European Research Council
status_note: Project period: 1 September 2017 to 29 February 2024.

document_title: REMOCEAN — Remotely Sensed Biogeochemical Cycles in the Ocean
notes: The European Union funded REMOCEAN to reduce uncertainty in biologically mediated ocean carbon fluxes using profiling floats, satellite observations and bio-optical modelling. The project examined the North Atlantic and subtropical gyres, regions with major but uncertain contributions to the global ocean carbon sink. It was completed as a research and observing programme and did not create an engineered carbon-removal intervention or a carbon-crediting system.
source: European Commission — CORDIS / Seventh Framework Programme
status_note: Project period: 1 June 2010 to 31 May 2016.

document_title: REOPTIMIZE — Remineralisation, Optics and Marine Particle Size
notes: The European Union funded REOPTIMIZE to estimate mesopelagic remineralisation from time-series observations of particle size and oxygen consumption collected by autonomous Bio-Argo platforms. The research improved spatial and temporal evidence on the biological carbon pump and ocean carbon budgets. It was completed as scientific research and did not establish an engineered sequestration project, statutory monitoring requirement or crediting methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS / Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions
status_note: Project period: 13 June 2016 to 12 June 2018.

document_title: Ocean artUp — Ocean Artificial Upwelling
notes: The European Research Council funded Ocean artUp to investigate artificial upwelling as a means of transporting nutrient-rich deep water to the surface. The project examined whether forced upwelling could support marine production, strengthen the biological carbon pump and contribute to deep-ocean carbon sequestration, while also assessing ecological and operational implications. It was completed as research and did not create a commercial deployment authorization, permit or verified carbon-removal programme.
source: European Commission — CORDIS / European Research Council
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2017 to 31 December 2021.

document_title: STTR Phase I — Bio-optical Sensor for the Direct Detection of Sinking Marine Particles
notes: The U.S. National Science Foundation provided a USD 254,110 STTR Phase I award to develop a bio-optical sensor for direct detection of sinking marine particles. The project used optical and housing-geometry modelling, laboratory testing and particle-collection analysis to improve measurement of carbon transported by the biological carbon pump. The award supported sensor development and did not establish an official MRV standard, authorize intentional ocean sequestration or verify carbon credits.
source: U.S. National Science Foundation — Small Business Technology Transfer Program
status_note: Award period: 1 January 2022 to 31 December 2022.

document_title: STEMM-CCS — Strategies for Environmental Monitoring of Marine Carbon Capture and Storage
notes: The European Union funded STEMM-CCS to develop and test strategies, technologies and best practices for detecting, monitoring and assessing potential leakage from offshore geological carbon-dioxide storage sites. The project supported environmental risk assessment and monitoring capability for marine geological storage. It was completed as research and method development and did not itself issue a storage permit, authorize a commercial injection project or certify stored carbon.
source: European Commission — CORDIS / Horizon 2020
status_note: Project period: 1 March 2016 to 29 February 2020.

document_title: CARBOCHANGE — Changes in Carbon Uptake and Emissions by Oceans in a Changing Climate
notes: The European Union funded CARBOCHANGE to improve observation, modelling and prediction of ocean carbon uptake and emissions under a changing climate. The programme integrated measurements and models to reduce uncertainty in air-sea carbon exchange and future ocean-sink behaviour. It was completed as a scientific research programme and did not establish an engineered carbon-removal project, regulatory standard or carbon-crediting mechanism.
source: European Commission — CORDIS / Seventh Framework Programme
status_note: Project period: 1 March 2011 to 28 February 2015.

document_title: PhytoSwim — In Situ Microfluidics to Study Phytoplankton Interactions Affecting Global Carbon Capture and Coral Nutrition
notes: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie project will develop in-situ microfluidic methods to study phytoplankton interactions that influence marine carbon capture and coral nutrition. The work is designed to improve understanding of microscale biological processes linking primary production, marine food webs and the biological carbon pump. The project had not started as of August 2026 and does not constitute a carbon-removal deployment, restoration programme, MRV standard or carbon-credit activity.
source: European Commission — CORDIS / Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions
status_note: EC signature date: 2 May 2025; planned project period: 1 September 2026 to 30 November 2028.

document_title: DAPOP — Deposition of Atmospheric Particles on the Ocean: A Process Study
notes: The FP7 project examined how atmospheric particles release iron and phosphorus after deposition on the surface ocean and how those nutrient inputs affect the efficiency of the biological carbon pump. Experiments focused on the northeastern tropical Atlantic, a region receiving substantial desert-dust deposition. The project studied natural biogeochemical processes and did not authorize or conduct deliberate commercial ocean fertilization, issue carbon credits or establish a deployment pathway.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 May 2009 to 31 August 2010; the project is closed.

document_title: CARAMBA — Unravelling the Microbial Carbon Pump in the Ocean
notes: The Horizon 2020 project investigated the taxonomic, genomic and metabolic mechanisms through which marine bacteria produce refractory dissolved organic matter. It combined bacterial cultures, organic-matter characterisation and genomic and transcriptomic analysis to clarify how the microbial carbon pump contributes to long-term ocean carbon storage. The project was terminated before its scheduled end and did not establish a microbial engineering deployment, verified removal quantity or crediting method.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 6 March 2017 to 5 March 2019; CORDIS records termination on 27 January 2019.

document_title: IMOS — Imaging Ocean Sinkers for Evaluating Carbon Export Fluxes
notes: The Horizon 2020 project used high-resolution underwater imaging, autonomous sampling, particle collection and simulation tools to improve estimates of biological-carbon-pump export. It linked optical particle properties with direct carbon-flux measurements to reduce uncertainty in ocean carbon-sequestration assessments. The project developed scientific measurement capability and did not create a statutory MRV standard, authorize engineered sequestration or verify commercial carbon removals.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 September 2022 to 31 August 2025; the project is closed.

document_title: EQUIP — Elemental Quota in Marine Phytoplankton for Effective Carbon Sequestration
notes: The Horizon 2020 fellowship examined elemental quotas in marine phytoplankton and their implications for carbon sequestration, biogeochemical modelling and biological production. The project sought improved process understanding for representing phytoplankton carbon and nutrient relationships. It was a scientific research award and did not constitute a microalgae deployment programme, quantify durable additional removals or certify carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 7 May 2015 to 6 May 2017; the project is closed.

document_title: AI-PhytoClim — AI Analysis of Phytoplankton Change and Regional Ocean CO2 Fluxes
notes: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie project applies artificial-intelligence methods to evaluate how climate-driven physical changes alter phytoplankton functional groups, productivity, surface-ocean carbon dioxide partial pressure and regional air-sea CO2 fluxes in the southwestern Atlantic. The project strengthens observation and modelling of a major ocean carbon-sink region. It does not create an engineered carbon-removal activity, mandatory accounting rule or carbon-credit programme.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 September 2025 to 31 August 2027; the project is active.

document_title: BIPHA — Bio-Physical Processes around Marine Snow Aggregates
notes: The Horizon 2020 project investigated flow, diffusion, particle scavenging and transparent exopolymeric-particle effects within marine-snow aggregates. These aggregates are an important pathway transporting diatom-derived organic carbon from surface waters toward the deep ocean. Advanced microscopy, particle-image velocimetry and microsensors were used to clarify biological-carbon-pump processes. The work did not involve intentional biomass sinking, deployment authorization or carbon-credit issuance.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 November 2015 to 18 December 2018; the project is closed.

document_title: PROCES — Production and Removal of Dissolved Organic Matter in Contrasting Oceanic Environments
notes: The FP6 project examined how dissolved organic carbon is produced and removed across productive and oligotrophic ocean environments. It investigated phytoplankton release, grazing, cell lysis, particle dissolution, bacterial processing and differences in dissolved-organic-matter bioreactivity. The work improved understanding of dissolved-carbon cycling and potential long-term storage but did not establish a microbial negative-emissions technology or a verified removal methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 5 July 2005 to 4 July 2006; the project is closed.

document_title: CARBON EXPORT — New Approaches for Understanding Oceanic Carbon Uptake
notes: The FP7 project evaluated oceanic carbon fixation and export using nitrogen-fixation measurements and naturally occurring radioisotopes to estimate downward carbon flux. It identified substantial export associated with both diatoms and unicellular diazotrophs and contributed evidence for global carbon-cycle models. The project addressed natural biological-pump processes and did not authorize ocean fertilization, establish an engineering project or issue credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 October 2008 to 30 September 2009; the project is closed.

document_title: FlocDOM — Dissolved Organic Matter and Flocculates in Arctic Coastal Ecosystems
notes: The Horizon 2020 project studied how dissolved organic matter from glaciers and thawing soils is degraded, flocculated, mineralised or buried in Greenland coastal ecosystems. It followed carbon pathways through bacteria, protists and benthic filter feeders and assessed whether increased terrestrial carbon inputs may shift the Arctic coastal ocean toward a carbon source or sink. It was completed research and did not establish a removal project or crediting method.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 February 2019 to 16 February 2022; the project is closed.

document_title: PALEOCARB — Role of the Marine Carbon Cycle in the Climate System
notes: The FP7 project combined marine-sediment geochemistry, biomarker proxies and coupled climate-carbon modelling to reconstruct organic-carbon sources, export and burial during the Holocene, Pliocene and Last Glacial Maximum. It assessed how marine carbon-cycle processes influenced atmospheric CO2 under different climatic states. The project was palaeoclimate research and did not represent engineered carbon removal or a policy accounting mechanism.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 July 2009 to 31 December 2011; the project is closed.

document_title: CARBOOCEAN — Marine Carbon Sources and Sinks Assessment
notes: The FP6 integrated project combined large-scale observations, process studies and advanced models to quantify marine carbon sources and sinks, especially in the Atlantic and Southern Oceans. It aimed to reduce uncertainty in annual air-sea CO2 fluxes, explain deep-water carbon transport and assess climate feedbacks affecting future ocean uptake. It produced research infrastructure and carbon budgets but did not create an engineered-removal deployment or carbon-credit system.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2005 to 31 December 2009; the project is closed.

document_title: ORFOIS — Origin and Fate of Biogenic Particle Fluxes in the Ocean
notes: The FP5 project quantified how biogenic particles are transformed into dissolved substances in the ocean water column and how particle, sediment, carbonate and nutrient processes affect ocean carbon sources and sinks. It developed community models, observation databases and coupled ocean-carbon simulations, including exploratory sequestration and iron-fertilisation scenarios. The project was modelling and assessment research and did not authorize or implement ocean fertilization.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 December 2001 to 30 November 2004; the project is closed.

document_title: Marine Dissolved Organic Matter Production and Plankton Ecological Interactions
notes: The FP4 project measured dissolved-organic-carbon production, composition and size structure in relation to phytoplankton physiological state and zooplankton grazing. It examined the efficiency of the dissolved-organic-carbon pump as an export and potential atmospheric-carbon-sequestration mechanism. The work was a short scientific fellowship and did not establish a microbial engineering project, a durable removal claim or carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 October 1998 to 30 September 1999; the project is closed.

document_title: ECODOM — Carbon Cycling and Coloured Dissolved Organic Matter in European Coastal Ecosystems
notes: The FP7 project integrated field observations, remote sensing and modelling to study dissolved-organic-matter sources, quality, transformation and carbon fluxes in eastern Mediterranean wetlands and coastal waters. It examined how climate, land use, hydrology and watershed management affect land-ocean carbon transfers and coastal ecosystem functioning. The project generated scientific evidence and did not establish a restoration programme, verified removal method or carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 May 2008 to 30 April 2012; the project is closed.

document_title: Dissolved Organic Matter in Ocean Ecosystems and the Biological Pump
notes: The INTAS project evaluated dissolved-organic-matter production, degradation and seasonal variability in open and coastal oceans and modelled its contribution to particulate and dissolved biological-pump fluxes. It also simulated ocean responses to warming, ultraviolet radiation, river inputs and excess atmospheric CO2. The project refined scientific estimates of ocean carbon uptake and did not constitute a deployment or market mechanism.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 March 1998 to 28 February 2001; the project is closed.

document_title: Global Carbon Cycle II, Part C: Ocean
notes: The FP3 project quantified anthropogenic CO2 absorption by the ocean using ship observations, satellite measurements, air-sea gas-exchange studies, dissolved-organic-carbon measurements and regional and global ocean models. It investigated seasonal ocean sources and sinks and the internal marine carbon cycle. The work was observational and modelling research and did not establish an engineered-removal intervention or crediting standard.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 1993 to 31 December 1995; the project is closed.

document_title: COMFORT — Coupled Ocean Carbon, Oxygen and Nutrient Cycles and Safe Operating Spaces
notes: The Horizon 2020 project quantified coupled ocean carbon, oxygen and nutrient cycles to identify climate-related tipping risks and safe operating spaces. It integrated observations and Earth-system modelling to assess future ocean conditions and mitigation pathways. The project supported scientific and policy assessment but did not authorize a marine carbon-removal technology, establish project-level MRV or issue credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 September 2019 to 31 August 2023; the project is closed.

document_title: CYCLOCARB — Oceanic Carbon Cycling Response to Global Temperature Changes
notes: The Horizon 2020 project developed a semi-empirical framework connecting ocean carbon cycling with global temperature changes using palaeoclimate databases, proxies and carbon partitioning among the ocean, atmosphere and solid Earth. It examined natural analogues for understanding anthropogenic carbon-cycle perturbation. The completed project was climate and carbon-cycle research and did not establish an engineered removal activity or carbon-accounting rule.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 April 2020 to 1 May 2023; the project is closed.

document_title: Dissolved Organic Nitrogen Pathways and Ocean Carbon Sequestration
notes: The FP4 project examined biologically active dissolved organic nitrogen as an intermediate in ocean carbon sequestration. Isotopic tracing was used to quantify excretion, biodegradation and food-web transfers and to determine how active dissolved-organic-matter pools contribute to exportable production and carbon storage. The work was fundamental research and did not constitute a removal-engineering project or verified accounting methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 July 1996 to 30 June 1997; the project is closed.

document_title: Global Carbon Cycle and Its Perturbation by Man and Climate
notes: The FP2 programme assessed regional carbon-dioxide sources and sinks, storage capacities and the response of the global carbon cycle to climatic change. Its ocean components addressed air-sea exchange, surface-ocean carbon-system dynamics and internal ocean processes alongside atmospheric, terrestrial and palaeoclimate work. The project produced integrated scientific assessment and did not represent an ocean-engineering deployment, permit or carbon-credit mechanism.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 July 1991 to 30 June 1993; the project is closed.

document_title: MIMEPOC — Microbially Mediated Particulate Organic Carbon Flux
notes: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie project examined how particle-associated prokaryotes control the formation, transformation and degradation of sinking particulate organic matter. It used metatranscriptomics, metagenomics, metaproteomics and stable-isotope methods to characterise microbial functions, carbon uptake and colonisation on particles at different depths. The completed project strengthened understanding of the biological carbon pump but did not establish an engineered sequestration activity, regulatory MRV standard or verified carbon-removal claim.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 June 2023 to 31 July 2025; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: BacPac — Bacterial Degradation of Marine Particles and Vertical Carbon Export
notes: The FP7 project investigated how heterotrophic bacteria colonise and degrade suspended and sinking marine particles and how those processes regulate vertical organic-carbon export. Sampling covered Mediterranean, North Norwegian and European Arctic waters and combined sediment traps with molecular analysis of particle-associated microbial communities. The project was completed as fundamental research and did not constitute biomass sinking, ocean fertilization, a carbon-credit methodology or deployment authorization.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 November 2012 to 31 October 2014.

document_title: European Microbiology of Particulate Systems
notes: The FP3 project examined microbial communities attached to marine particles in the north-western Mediterranean and their role in water-column biogeochemistry. It compared attached and free-living bacteria, measured microbial activity and particle-associated budgets and used the results to model carbon flux, remineralisation and particle distributions. The programme was completed research and did not create a carbon-removal engineering project, monitoring obligation or crediting mechanism.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 September 1994 to 31 August 1996.

document_title: O2ZOOM — Ocean Oxygen Loss, Zooplankton Behaviour and the Carbon Cycle
notes: The planned Marie Skłodowska-Curie project will investigate how declining oxygen concentrations alter krill migration and therefore zooplankton-mediated carbon export. Laboratory incubations, acoustic observations in a Norwegian fjord and individual-based ecological modelling will be used to quantify changes in carbon transport from surface waters. The project had not started as of 6 August 2026 and does not constitute a removal deployment, restoration programme or carbon-credit activity.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: EC signature date: 4 April 2025; planned project period: 1 September 2026 to 31 August 2028.

document_title: REFINE — Robots Explore Plankton-Driven Fluxes in the Marine Twilight Zone
notes: The European Research Council funded REFINE to quantify physical, biological and biogeochemical controls on the biological carbon pump in the ocean twilight zone. The project developed vertically profiling robotic floats, conducted multi-year observations in contrasting ocean regions and used artificial intelligence to upscale regional carbon-flux processes. It is an observational research programme and does not authorize engineered ocean sequestration or certify carbon removals.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 October 2019 to 30 September 2026.

document_title: NIPROFEED — Nitrogen Fixation, Primary Production and Ocean Carbon Export
notes: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie project examined feedbacks among nitrogen-fixing microorganisms, primary production, particle formation, carbon export and oxygen depletion. It tested whether diazotroph-derived nitrogen can amplify particle production and strengthen a feedback loop affecting the biological carbon pump and ocean health. The project ended in 2026 and did not authorize nutrient addition, establish an ocean-fertilization programme or certify carbon removals.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 May 2024 to 30 April 2026.

document_title: QSIPP — Bacterial Quorum Sensing and Marine Particle Degradation
notes: The Horizon 2020 project investigated whether bacterial quorum-sensing signals regulate hydrolytic proteins, particle degradation and the efficiency of particulate-organic-carbon export. Its methods included mass spectrometry, proteomics, three-dimensional particle imaging and molecular analysis of particle-associated bacterial communities. The project was terminated in 2016 and did not produce a deployment authorization, official MRV methodology or verified carbon-removal outcome.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: EC signature date: 24 April 2015; CORDIS records project termination on 17 March 2016.

document_title: MicroSymb — Seagrass, Sponge and Microbiome Resilience under Ocean Warming
notes: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie project studies the association between Posidonia oceanica, the sponge Chondrilla nucula and their microbial communities. Field sampling, mesocosm experiments, stable-isotope probing and meta-omics are used to determine whether nutrient and microbial exchanges improve the resilience of a major Mediterranean blue-carbon habitat under thermal stress. It is an active research project and does not itself restore seagrass, quantify additional removal or issue carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 September 2025 to 31 August 2027.

document_title: OCEAN-CERTAIN — Ocean Food-Web Patrol and Biological Carbon-Pump Uncertainty
notes: The FP7 project assessed how climate change and human pressures alter marine food webs and the efficiency of natural ocean carbon uptake and deposition. It combined data mining, mesocosm and microcosm experiments, cruises, ecosystem modelling, socio-economic scenarios and decision-support tools across Arctic, Mediterranean and Patagonian systems. The programme supported policy-relevant assessment of biological and microbial carbon pumps but did not authorize engineered removal or create credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 November 2013 to 31 October 2017.

document_title: PALAEOCON — Conservation Palaeobiology of Terrestrial and Marine Carbon Sinks
notes: The Horizon 2020 project used palaeoecological records to reconstruct long-term changes in Iberian seagrass meadows and peatlands. Dating, sedimentology, geochemistry, palynology and numerical analysis were intended to identify historical baselines, tipping points and drivers affecting carbon-storage resilience and conservation priorities. CORDIS records early termination in 2020. The project did not establish a restoration programme, accounting standard or carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project started on 1 September 2019 and was terminated on 30 June 2020.

document_title: EMMA — Enhancing Mangrove Restoration through Microtopographic Analysis
notes: The planned Marie Skłodowska-Curie project will investigate how fine-scale topography and hydrology control mangrove seedling retention, establishment and survival. UAV LiDAR, hyperspectral surveys, field experiments and biophysical modelling will be used to identify high-potential restoration areas and improve long-term restoration success. The project had not started as of August 2026 and therefore does not represent completed restoration, verified carbon sequestration or issued credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: EC signature date: 30 March 2026; planned project period: 1 February 2027 to 31 January 2030.

document_title: CREC — Coastal Research Network on Environmental Changes
notes: The FP7 network examined climate and land-use pressures on mangrove forests through an international exchange programme, a mangrove reference database, physiological and population studies and ecosystem modelling. Its results included evidence that mangrove crabs can enhance soil aeration and mangrove carbon sequestration. The project was completed research and collaboration; it did not create a restoration target, carbon-accounting method or verified crediting programme.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 June 2010 to 31 May 2014.

document_title: BLUESURVEY — Underwater Satellite Technology for Seagrass Blue-Carbon Monitoring
notes: The European Innovation Council funded development of an underwater hyperspectral mapping platform for seagrass meadows and other seafloor applications. The project combined underwater imaging, precise navigation and artificial-intelligence processing to map seagrass condition and estimate stored carbon, with the stated aim of reducing verification costs for restoration and carbon-credit projects. The project closed in 2024 and did not itself certify a methodology, issue credits or prove additional carbon removal.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 May 2022 to 30 April 2024; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: SMART — Sponge Microbiome Adaptation and Resilience to Thermal Stress
notes: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie project investigates how sponge-associated microorganisms respond to thermal stress and contribute to host resilience. Marine sponges influence carbon cycling and sequestration through microbial processing of dissolved and particulate organic matter, and the project combines experiments, microbiome analysis and ecological monitoring to support conservation under ocean warming. It is active research and does not constitute an engineered carbon-removal activity, restoration permit or crediting methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2027.

document_title: MARIX — Methane and Ammonium Removal in Marine Redox Transition Zones
notes: The European Research Council funded MARIX to identify microbial pathways that remove methane and ammonium in marine redox transition zones. The project combines field observations, geochemical measurements, isotope tracing and microbial analyses to determine how these processes regulate marine carbon and nitrogen cycling and limit greenhouse-gas release. It is active fundamental research and does not constitute carbon-dioxide removal deployment, a carbon-credit programme or a regulatory standard.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 March 2020 to 31 August 2027.

document_title: DOMAINE — Dissolved Organic Matter in Coastal Ecosystems: Transport, Dynamics and Environmental Impact
notes: The FP5 project investigated the transport, storage and cycling of dissolved organic carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus from land into coastal ecosystems across four climatic zones. It combined field studies, experiments and modelling to assess how land use, hydrology and autochthonous production affect coastal dissolved organic matter and environmental management. The project was completed as scientific research and did not establish a carbon-removal engineering activity, crediting methodology or deployment authorization.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2001 to 31 December 2003.

document_title: CarbEx — Tracing Carbon Exchanges and Fluxes between Arctic and Atlantic Basins
notes: The Horizon 2020 project traced freshwater and terrestrial dissolved-organic-carbon fluxes from the Arctic Ocean through the Fram Strait into the Atlantic. It integrated oceanographic expeditions, satellite ocean-colour observations and numerical modelling and developed optical approaches for monitoring freshwater and carbon dynamics. The project was completed as research and technology development and did not create a negative-emissions project, regulatory MRV standard or carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 November 2019 to 31 October 2021.

document_title: CHARMAD — Chemical Characterisation and Cycling of Marine Dissolved Organic Matter
notes: The FP6 project examined the molecular composition, biological production, degradation, bioavailability and export of marine dissolved organic matter. Advanced chemical and molecular-biological methods were used to determine how dissolved organic carbon is transferred from surface waters to the deep ocean and contributes to one of Earth's largest carbon reservoirs. The project did not establish a microbial engineering deployment, certified methodology or verified removal quantity.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 March 2004 to 28 February 2006.

document_title: DIASIN — Integrative Eco-Mechanics of Diatom Sinking and the Biological Carbon Pump
notes: The FP7 project investigated how diatom physiology, sinking behaviour and small-scale fluid dynamics influence the transfer of photosynthetically fixed carbon from surface waters to the deep ocean. It treated phytoplankton as active participants in the biological carbon pump and linked organism responses with environmental change and biogeochemical cycles. The completed research did not authorize ocean fertilization, biomass sinking or carbon-credit issuance.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2012 to 31 December 2015.

document_title: DIADOM — Interactions between Nitrogen-Fixers and Dissolved Organic Matter in the Ocean
notes: The FP7 project studied autotrophic and heterotrophic marine nitrogen-fixing microorganisms and their interactions with dissolved organic matter in illuminated and dark-ocean environments. It addressed previously unaccounted nitrogen inputs, microbial nutrition and consequences for primary production and ocean carbon cycling. The project was completed as fundamental research and did not constitute nutrient fertilization, engineered carbon removal or a crediting system.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 March 2014 to 29 February 2016.

document_title: PHY-GO — Phytoplankton Community Structure and Carbon Export Using BGC-Argo Floats
notes: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie project linked direct measurements of phytoplankton community structure with bio-optical observations from biogeochemical Argo floats. Flow cytometry, optical proxies and machine learning were used to estimate group-specific biomass and evaluate how phytoplankton composition affects carbon export to the mesopelagic ocean. The project was completed as research and did not establish an official MRV methodology, engineered sequestration activity or carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 June 2023 to 31 May 2025.

document_title: SEAMLESS — Services Based on Ecosystem Data Assimilation: Essential Science and Solutions
notes: The Horizon 2020 project developed an ecosystem-data-assimilation prototype for the Copernicus Marine Environment Monitoring Service. It integrated satellite, biogeochemical-Argo, glider and model data to improve operational indicators including plankton phenology and particulate carbon export. The project strengthened ocean monitoring and forecasting but did not establish a carbon-removal project, mandatory verification standard or crediting methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2021 to 31 December 2023.

document_title: CONSUMALG — Microbial Uptake and Degradation of Marine Macroalgal Biomass
notes: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie project studies microbial degradation of Saccharina latissima and traces carbon flow from kelp biomass into dissolved organic matter and bacterial communities. Multi-omics, isotope tracing and nanoSIMS methods are being used to identify primary and secondary degraders and quantify their contribution to coastal marine carbon cycling. The active project does not constitute macroalgae sinking, a deployment permit, verified removal or carbon-credit issuance.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 February 2026 to 31 January 2028.

document_title: SPICE — Submesoscale Processes in a Changing Environment
notes: The Horizon 2020 project quantified how small-scale upper-ocean processes influence air-sea heat and carbon exchange in the Southern Ocean. It combined autonomous marine robot observations with ultra-high-resolution numerical models to assess carbon flux variability and storage in the ocean interior. The project was completed as research and did not establish engineered removal, a project-level accounting methodology or carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 August 2021 to 31 July 2023.

document_title: SO-CHIC — Southern Ocean Carbon and Heat Impact on Climate
notes: The Horizon 2020 project quantified Southern Ocean heat and carbon budgets and the processes controlling exchanges among the atmosphere, ocean and sea ice. It combined dedicated observations, long-term time series and advanced modelling, including study of the Weddell Polynya and implications for global climate projections and stocktakes. The project was completed as coordinated scientific assessment and did not authorize engineered ocean carbon removal or create a crediting mechanism.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 November 2019 to 31 October 2024.

document_title: SOCCLI — The Role of the Southern Ocean Carbon Cycle under Climate Change
notes: The FP7 project investigated the physical and biogeochemical processes governing the Southern Ocean carbon sink and its response to climate change. It used observations and modelling to improve understanding of carbon uptake, circulation, ecosystem processes and future feedbacks. The completed project supported climate and ocean-carbon assessment and did not constitute an engineered carbon-removal activity, deployment authorization or carbon-credit programme.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 August 2012 to 31 July 2016.

document_title: ZINCCARB — Zinc Isotopes as Tracers of Nutrient Cycling and Carbon Uptake by Past Oceans
notes: The FP6 project used zinc isotopes to investigate past nutrient cycling, biological productivity and ocean carbon uptake. It addressed how the biological pump transferred carbon to the deep ocean and influenced atmospheric carbon dioxide during Quaternary climate changes. The project was completed as palaeoceanographic research and did not create an ocean-fertilization activity, monitoring standard or carbon-credit method.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2007 to 31 December 2008.

document_title: LAC — Liquid-Aperture Coulter Counter for Sizing Oceanic Particles and Phytoplankton
notes: The FP7 project developed particle-sizing technology for marine particles and phytoplankton. Particle size affects settling, aggregation, remineralisation, carbon biomass and the efficiency of the biological pump and also determines optical signals used for satellite monitoring. The project was completed as sensor and measurement research and did not establish a statutory MRV standard, engineered sequestration project or verified carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 March 2011 to 28 February 2015.

document_title: SCOOBi — Seeking Constraints on Open Ocean Biocalcification
notes: The European Research Council project investigates environmental and biological controls on calcification by coccolithophores and foraminifera, organisms that convert carbon into calcium carbonate and strongly influence the ocean carbonate system. It combines genetics, metabolomics, physiology, isotope geochemistry and sediment records to quantify modern and past pelagic calcification. The active project does not constitute engineered mineralisation deployment, a carbon-credit methodology or verified removal.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 December 2022 to 30 November 2027.

document_title: SOSiC — Southern Ocean Silicon Cycling Using Modern and Palaeoceanographic Isotope Records
notes: The Horizon 2020 project investigated silicon cycling and its connection to diatom productivity, biological carbon export and atmospheric carbon dioxide in the Southern Ocean. Modern seawater measurements and high-resolution sediment-core isotope records were used to reconstruct nutrient transport and carbon-cycle changes over the last 150,000 years. The completed project was scientific research and did not authorize ocean fertilization or certify carbon removals.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 April 2016 to 31 March 2018.

document_title: CARBONSINK — Life beneath the Ocean Floor: The Subsurface Sink of Carbon in the Marine Environment
notes: The European Research Council funded CARBONSINK to determine the fate of dissolved inorganic carbon produced in marine sediments and oceanic crust. The project combined experiments, geochemical measurements and numerical modelling to constrain whether subsurface carbon diffuses back to the ocean or precipitates as carbonate minerals. The research was relevant to evaluating long-term marine subsurface storage, but it did not authorize carbon injection, establish a storage permit or verify an engineered removal project.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 December 2012 to 30 November 2017; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: ECO2 — Sub-Seabed CO2 Storage: Impact on Marine Ecosystems
notes: The FP7 ECO2 project assessed leakage risks and ecological impacts associated with sub-seabed carbon dioxide storage. It examined operating and potential storage sites, applied monitoring technologies, studied natural seep analogues and developed a best-practice guide covering site management, environmental monitoring, remediation and the precautionary principle. The project supported risk assessment and governance of offshore storage but did not itself issue a storage permit or certify stored carbon.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 May 2011 to 30 April 2015; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: RISCS — Research into Impacts and Safety in CO2 Storage
notes: The FP7 RISCS project generated evidence for safe management of geological carbon-storage sites by quantifying the environmental effects of exposure to known carbon dioxide fluxes. Field and laboratory experiments, natural-leakage observations and numerical simulations covered both marine and terrestrial ecosystems and supported environmental-impact assessment over different timescales. The project did not authorize a storage site, approve a marine injection activity or certify stored carbon.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2010 to 31 December 2013; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: EPOCA — European Project on Ocean Acidification
notes: The FP7 EPOCA project documented changes in ocean chemistry and biogeography, reconstructed past variability and quantified biological and ecosystem responses to ocean acidification. It integrated laboratory and field experiments with biogeochemical, sediment and coupled ocean-climate models and assessed risks, thresholds and carbon-cycle feedbacks. The project strengthened the scientific basis for ocean-acidification policy but did not constitute ocean alkalinity enhancement, authorize material addition or verify carbon removal.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 May 2008 to 30 April 2012; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: SEA-THROUGH — Novel In Situ Imaging Technology to Explore the Ladder of Vertical Migrations to the Deep Sea
notes: The European Research Council funded SEA-THROUGH to develop advanced imaging technology for studying vertically migrating organisms and food-web connectivity from surface waters to depths of up to 6,000 metres. These migrations influence deep-sea biodiversity, organic-carbon transport and the functioning of the deep ocean as a carbon sink. The active project is observational research and does not establish an engineered sequestration pathway, deployment authorization or carbon-credit methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 September 2024 to 31 August 2029.

document_title: REDRESS — Restoration of Deep-Sea Habitats to Rebuild European Seas
notes: The Horizon Europe REDRESS project develops and tests restoration approaches for degraded deep-sea habitats, including sea-pen fields, bamboo corals, coral gardens, cold-water coral reefs, sponge fields and cold seeps. It maps damaged areas and refugia, evaluates active and passive restoration and links ecological outcomes with carbon sequestration, climate mitigation and socio-economic value. The project supports demonstration and policy development but does not itself certify carbon credits or authorize commercial carbon-removal deployment.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 February 2024 to 31 January 2028.

document_title: HEALSEA — Innovative Indicators of Resilience to Protect Seagrass Meadows
notes: The Horizon 2020 HEALSEA project tested ecological indicators intended to provide early warning of declining seagrass resilience. Experimental and theoretical work examined critical slowing down, recovery from disturbance and response trajectories under increasing stress, with the aim of producing practical conservation tools. The project was terminated in 2020 and did not establish a restoration programme, quantify additional carbon removal or issue blue-carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 9 April 2018 to 11 October 2020; CORDIS records termination on 31 August 2020.

document_title: SEGRALCS — Predictive Tool of Seagrass Health for Low-Crested Coastal Structures
notes: The Horizon Europe SEGRALCS project developed a quantitative prediction approach for integrating seagrass health into the design of low-crested coastal structures and breakwaters. It focused on Cymodocea nodosa and Posidonia oceanica and examined hydrodynamic, sediment-transport and ecological effects relevant to conserving Mediterranean seagrass habitats and their carbon-storage function. The project was terminated in 2025 and did not authorize restoration, establish a carbon-credit methodology or verify additional removal.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 May 2023 to 31 October 2025; CORDIS records termination on 1 January 2025.

document_title: SEAPAID — Seagrass Production and Isotopic Discrimination
notes: The FP6 SEAPAID project studied seagrass production, carbon and nitrogen content and isotopic discrimination in relation to environmental conditions. Isotopic signatures were used to trace carbon and nitrogen flows between source and sink systems and to improve understanding of seagrass ecosystem structure and dynamics. The project was completed as scientific research and did not establish a restoration programme, verified blue-carbon accounting method or crediting mechanism.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 October 2004 to 30 September 2006; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: BIOSHARE — Bacterial Interactions in One-Carbon Cycling and the Marine Carbon Cycle
notes: The FP7 BIOSHARE project investigated cooperation among heterotrophic marine bacteria involved in cycling one-carbon compounds and the consequences of these interactions for marine carbon processing. It examined microbial pathways that are usually represented incompletely in ocean-carbon models. The project was completed as fundamental microbiological research and did not establish microbial carbon-removal engineering, a deployment programme or verified carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 May 2014 to 30 April 2017; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: MARINEGLYCAN — Marine Chemical Glycobiology and Molecular Carbon Cycling
notes: The Horizon 2020 MARINEGLYCAN project developed chemical-biology tools for tracing the production, transformation and biological functions of sulfated marine glycans. Because marine microalgae channel substantial carbon into carbohydrates, the project sought molecular-level understanding of carbon flow from individual enzymes to interacting microbial communities. The project was completed as research and did not establish a marine glycan sequestration technology, verified removal quantity or crediting standard.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 August 2021 to 31 July 2023; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: MYCO-CARB — Functional Biology and Ecology of Planktonic Marine Fungi in the Carbon Cycle
notes: The European Research Council funded MYCO-CARB to determine the functional roles of marine planktonic fungi in coastal waters, the open ocean and marine-snow particles. The programme examined fungal biomass, saprotrophic activity and contributions to decomposition, particle processing and the biological carbon pump. The project was completed as fundamental research and did not create a fungal carbon-removal technology, deployment authorization or carbon-credit methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 May 2018 to 31 October 2024; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: M&MS — Monitoring and Managing European Seagrass Beds
notes: The FP5 M&MS project defined habitat requirements, pressures, resilience indicators and recovery processes for European seagrass ecosystems. It combined databases, field surveys and experiments to produce monitoring plans, early-warning indicators and management strategies for seagrass conservation. Although seagrass meadows are blue-carbon habitats, the project did not quantify additional carbon removal, establish a carbon-credit methodology or implement a specific restoration project.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 January 2001 to 30 June 2004; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: SEAMET — Multi-Driver Climate Change Effects on Seagrass Metabolism
notes: The Horizon 2020 SEAMET project investigated how ocean acidification, warming and hypoxia affect carbon incorporation, photosynthetic physiology, metabolic balance and acclimation in seagrasses and associated communities. The project used seagrass as a model habitat for scaling organism-level responses to ecosystem functioning and carbon metabolism. It was completed as scientific research and did not establish a restoration programme, accounting method or verified blue-carbon removal.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 8 January 2018 to 7 January 2020; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: CAENEUS — Crenarchaeota Ecology and Nutrient Utilisation in the Subsurface Ocean
notes: The FP7 CAENEUS project examined marine Crenarchaeota and bacteria responsible for ammonia oxidation and dark carbon dioxide fixation in the deep Atlantic Ocean. It quantified gene abundance, nitrification and chemoautotrophic carbon-fixation rates across depth gradients and contrasting water masses. The completed research improved understanding of microbial carbon fixation in the dark ocean and did not constitute microbial engineering, deployment authorization or a carbon-credit methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 June 2010 to 31 May 2012; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: SCrIPT — Stable Chromium Isotopes as a Productivity Tracer
notes: The European Research Council funded SCrIPT to develop stable chromium isotopes as a proxy for changes in marine export productivity and the strength of the biological carbon pump. The project combined phytoplankton cultures, water-column observations and sediment analyses to calibrate chromium-isotope fractionation and reconstruct past variations in ocean carbon export. It was completed as scientific proxy development and did not establish an engineered sequestration activity, statutory monitoring method or carbon-credit programme.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 May 2019 to 30 April 2025; CORDIS lists the project as closed.

document_title: GOSAC — Global Ocean Storage of Anthropogenic Carbon
notes: The FP4 GOSAC project compared and validated seven independently developed three-dimensional ocean carbon-cycle models and assessed global anthropogenic carbon storage. It also explored modelled deep-ocean carbon-dioxide disposal scenarios as a potential mitigation option. The completed project produced modelling and intercomparison tools and did not authorize ocean disposal, establish a permit pathway, verify stored carbon or create carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 December 1997 to 31 March 2001.

document_title: DEEPOCEANGLACIALCO2 — Deep-Sea Corals and Southern Ocean Carbon Regulation
notes: The FP7 fellowship used deep-sea corals from the Amundsen sector of the Southern Ocean to test how deep-ocean circulation and ventilation influenced atmospheric carbon dioxide during glacial periods. Geochemical records from coral skeletons were used to reconstruct past water-mass changes and carbon storage. The project was completed as palaeoceanographic research and did not constitute engineered sequestration, a deployment authorization or a carbon-credit methodology.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 March 2008 to 28 February 2010.

document_title: ARCADIA — Archaeal Activity Dynamics in Marine Snow and Ambient Coastal Water
notes: The FP7 project compared archaeal activity in marine-snow particles and surrounding coastal seawater to clarify the contribution of particle-associated archaea to dark-ocean carbon and nutrient budgets. Molecular and activity measurements were used to examine previously underrepresented microbial processes linked to sinking particles and remineralisation. The project was completed as fundamental research and did not establish microbial carbon-removal engineering, a deployment programme or verified removals.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 15 January 2009 to 14 January 2011.

document_title: PCFLUCS — Plankton Community Structure, Seston Quality and Coastal Carbon Fluxes
notes: The FP6 fellowship quantified coastal pelagic carbon fluxes at the Gullmarsfjord and Río de la Plata, including grazing, predation and downward export by phytoplankton, faecal pellets, carcasses and marine snow. It tested how plankton community structure and seston quality regulate carbon-flow variability at seasonal and sub-seasonal scales. The research did not create an engineered-removal project, mandatory accounting method or carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 June 2006 to 31 May 2008. A related return-phase grant used a separate CORDIS identifier and was not added as a second database record to avoid duplicating the same research project.

document_title: PLOCEAN — Plastic Impacts on Ocean Biogeochemical Cycles in the Anthropocene
notes: The Horizon 2020 PLOCEAN project examined how microplastics interact with microbial communities, organic matrices and marine particles and how those interactions may alter carbon turnover, nutrient cycling, primary production and downward particle flux. It combined field observations, polymer characterisation, metagenomics, laboratory studies and citizen science. The project was terminated in 2023 and did not establish a carbon-removal activity, regulatory standard or verified sequestration outcome.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Planned project period: 5 July 2021 to 5 July 2025; CORDIS records termination on 31 August 2023.

document_title: EFFECTIVE — Protection and Restoration Management in Mediterranean Marine Protected Areas
notes: The Horizon Europe EFFECTIVE project applies ecosystem-based management, digital tools and nature-based solutions in four Mediterranean pilot areas. It includes real-environment demonstrations of seabed protection and restoration intended to preserve seabed carbon-sequestration capacity, while assessing legislation, connectivity, participation and social implications. The active project supports restoration and governance development but does not itself certify carbon credits or authorize commercial carbon removal.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 June 2023 to 31 May 2027.

document_title: RETRO-PUMP — Reconstruction of Global Redox Transitions and the Precambrian Biological Carbon Pump
notes: The European Research Council funded RETRO-PUMP to reconstruct how changes in the Precambrian biological carbon pump influenced ocean redox conditions and long-term carbon burial. The project uses geological records, geochemistry and process modelling to examine the evolution of carbon export and oxygenation over deep time. It is active fundamental research and does not constitute an engineered sequestration project, monitoring standard or carbon-credit mechanism.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2030.

document_title: SENSEOCEAN — Marine Sensors for the 21st Century
notes: The FP7 SENSEOCEAN project developed integrated, cost-effective in-situ sensors for marine biogeochemistry, including carbon dioxide and carbonate-system measurements. The programme combined microfabrication, self-calibration, system integration and mass-production approaches to improve large-scale ocean observation. It was completed as sensor research and demonstration and did not establish a statutory MRV requirement, authorize a marine CDR project or certify carbon removals.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 October 2013 to 30 September 2017.

document_title: CARBON14ARCTIC — Terrestrial Carbon Export to the Eurasian Arctic Shelf
notes: The FP7 project assessed the export, burial and degradation of terrestrial organic carbon released to the Eurasian Arctic Shelf under climate warming. It combined molecular characterisation, compound-specific radiocarbon analysis, water and sediment sampling and dated cores to distinguish black carbon and soil-derived material and quantify their fate. The project was completed as Arctic carbon-cycle research and did not establish engineered sequestration or carbon credits.
source: European Commission — CORDIS
status_note: Project period: 1 October 2008 to 30 September 2010.

document_title: BiPhySO — Biological and Physical Drivers of Southern Ocean Oxygen Budgets
notes: The Marie Skłodowska-Curie project uses dissolved-oxygen and particulate-backscatter sensors together with glider and autonomous-platform datasets from the Ross, Amundsen and Weddell Seas.
