notes: This Adaptation Fund project addressed coastal flooding, erosion, salinization and degradation of mangrove habitats affecting communities in Dionewar and Fadial within Senegal's Saloum estuary. It combined ecosystem-resilience measures with flood and salinity protection, support for fisheries, oyster farming and forestry livelihoods, local planning and knowledge management. Restoration and improved management of mangrove-dependent habitats were intended to rebuild protective ecosystem services and sustain community livelihoods. The intervention is relevant to blue-carbon conservation because mangrove degradation had reduced ecological function, but the programme's formal objective was adaptation rather than carbon-credit generation. The official project materials do not provide a verified carbon baseline, net removal calculation, registry registration or credit issuance, and carbon benefits remain ancillary to documented resilience outcomes.
source: Adaptation Fund / Centre de Suivi Ecologique (CSE), Senegal
status_note: Completed local adaptation project with multiple performance reports retained on the official Adaptation Fund page.

subnational_area: Mon Choisy, Riviere des Galets and Quatre Soeurs
document_title: Climate Change Adaptation Programme in the Coastal Zone of Mauritius
notes: This Adaptation Fund programme implemented coastal-protection measures in vulnerable locations in Mauritius using a combination of engineered infrastructure, mangroves and other shoreline vegetation, storm-surge warning systems, institutional training, policy mainstreaming and public information. Mangrove planting and shoreline vegetation were intended to reduce erosion and strengthen natural protection, while monitoring assessed the relationship between coastal processes, climate change and intervention effectiveness. The programme is relevant to ecological restoration and biological carbon storage but was designed primarily for adaptation and disaster-risk reduction. The official record does not present a project-level carbon baseline, additionality analysis, permanence requirement, blue-carbon methodology or credit issuance. Its documented policy contribution is integration of long-term climate risk into coastal planning and protection decisions.
source: Adaptation Fund / United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) / Government of Mauritius
status_note: Completed national coastal adaptation programme with a completion report and final evaluation listed on the official project page.

subnational_area: Rote Ndao and Sabu Raijua Districts, Savu Sea
document_title: Ecosystem-Based Adaptation to Support Climate Resilience in Rote Ndao and Sabu Raijua Districts in the Savu Sea
notes: This Adaptation Fund project supports ecosystem-based adaptation in small-island communities of Indonesia's Savu Sea through climate-risk information, local capacity building, resilient livelihoods and protection or restoration of coastal ecosystems. Project documentation identifies mangroves, seagrass beds and coral reefs as natural systems that reduce wave energy, stabilize coastlines, sustain fisheries and strengthen food security. Conservation and restoration of mangroves and seagrasses are directly relevant to coastal blue-carbon stocks, although the project's formal objective is adaptation rather than quantified carbon removal. The official project page does not report an approved blue-carbon methodology, project-level carbon baseline, additionality and permanence assessment, registry registration or credit issuance. Carbon benefits should therefore be treated as potential co-benefits of ecosystem recovery.
source: Adaptation Fund / Kemitraan / YAPEKA Consortium and Indonesian local partners
status_note: Approved Adaptation Fund project with project documents available from 2022; the official page does not report project closure.

document_title: Strengthening the Adaptive Capacity of Coastal Communities of Fiji to Climate Change through Nature-Based Seawalls
notes: This Adaptation Fund project combines mangrove forests, locally sourced boulders and vetiver grass to construct nature-based seawalls for sixteen climate-vulnerable coastal communities in Fiji. The programme also strengthens cross-ministerial coordination, engineering capacity, community participation, safeguards, maintenance arrangements and knowledge transfer so that similar interventions can be replicated elsewhere. The official project page records approval in April 2024, implementation beginning in May 2026 and expected completion in November 2031. Mangrove establishment and protection can conserve and increase biological carbon stocks, but the programme is formally an adaptation and coastal-protection investment. It does not establish a blue-carbon baseline, additionality test, crediting methodology, registry registration or verified carbon-credit issuance.
source: Adaptation Fund / Pacific Community / Government of Fiji
status_note: Approved on 19 April 2024 and officially listed as under implementation from 4 May 2026 to the expected completion date of 4 November 2031.

subnational_area: Selected coastal communities in both countries
document_title: Improved Resilience of Coastal Communities in Côte d’Ivoire and Ghana
notes: This regional Adaptation Fund programme supports coastal-risk assessment, planning, community resilience and green or hybrid infrastructure in Côte d’Ivoire and Ghana. Its nature-based portfolio includes protection and restoration of mangroves, seagrass planting and other coastal habitat interventions alongside livelihood support, institutional strengthening and regional knowledge exchange. The programme was approved in August 2023, began implementation in September 2024 and is scheduled to continue through March 2029. The ecosystem measures can conserve or rebuild coastal biological carbon stocks, but the programme is primarily designed for adaptation and protection from erosion, flooding and sea-level rise. Its public project materials do not establish a carbon-credit methodology, quantify verified net removals, register offsets or report issuance of tradable credits.
source: Adaptation Fund / UN-Habitat / Governments and partners of Côte d’Ivoire and Ghana
status_note: Approved on 28 August 2023 and officially listed as under implementation from 26 September 2024, with expected completion on 26 March 2029.

document_title: Enhancing the Resilience of Coastal Livelihoods through Marine Ecosystem-Based Adaptation on the Gulf of Thailand
notes: This Adaptation Fund concept proposes a five-year marine ecosystem-based adaptation programme for coastal communities around the Gulf of Thailand. The concept combines protection and restoration of mangroves, seagrass beds and coral reefs with climate-risk information, resilient livelihoods, institutional coordination and exploration of sustainable financing, including blue-carbon-related approaches and public-private cooperation. The requested grant is USD 10 million and the official project page identifies UNDP and Thailand's Department of Climate Change and Environment as the implementing and executing entities. The proposal remains at the concept-submission stage. It does not authorize restoration at a specific site, establish a national blue-carbon methodology, confirm project additionality or permanence, register carbon units or report verified removals and issued credits.
source: Adaptation Fund / United Nations Development Programme / Government of Thailand
status_note: Officially listed in 2026 as a submitted five-year project concept requesting USD 10 million; full approval and implementation had not been confirmed.

document_title: Enhancing Coastal Resilience in the South-East Asia Seas
notes: This regional Adaptation Fund concept proposes a six-year programme combining coastal observation, hazard prediction, early warning, decision support and nature-based restoration across participating South-East Asian countries. The institutional partnership includes national marine, meteorological and research agencies, UNESCO ocean-observation bodies, UNIDO and regional technical organizations. Proposed ecosystem measures address degraded coastal habitats, including mangrove and seagrass systems, while digital monitoring and forecasting are intended to guide site selection, evaluate resilience outcomes and improve disaster preparedness. The official page records a requested grant of approximately USD 29.3 million and a concept-submitted status. The proposal is not yet an implementation authorization or blue-carbon standard and does not establish verified removal quantities, credit eligibility, registry approval or carbon-credit issuance.
source: Adaptation Fund / United Nations Industrial Development Organization and regional partners
status_note: Listed in 2026 as a submitted regional concept requesting USD 29,324,647 for six years; final approval and implementation had not been reported.

document_title: Enhancing the Climate Resilience of Coastal Communities in Limón and Bocas del Toro through Nature-Based Solutions for Local Livelihoods
notes: This endorsed regional Adaptation Fund concept targets the connected coastal landscape of Limón in Costa Rica and Bocas del Toro in Panama. It proposes nature-based adaptation within a seagrass, coral and mangrove ecosystem mosaic, combined with climate-risk information, local livelihood measures, community participation and transboundary coordination. The programme requests USD 12.1 million for a four-year implementation period and is to be implemented by UNEP with national executing partners. Endorsement permits preparation of a fuller proposal but does not constitute final financing approval or authorization of individual restoration activities. The concept does not provide an approved blue-carbon accounting method, project-level additionality and permanence assessment, independently verified carbon removals, registry registration or evidence that carbon credits have been issued.
source: Adaptation Fund / United Nations Environment Programme / Costa Rican and Panamanian partners
status_note: Officially listed in 2026 as an endorsed four-year regional concept requesting USD 12.1 million; a complete approved implementation proposal was not shown.

document_title: Enhancing Adaptive Capacity of Communities to Climate Change-Related Floods in the North Coast and Islands Region of Papua New Guinea
notes: This completed Adaptation Fund project combined coastal and inland flood early-warning systems, preparedness planning, institutional strengthening and support for community-led mangrove reforestation and conservation. The coastal component created observation, information-management and response arrangements while enabling local mangrove projects to improve shoreline protection and ecosystem resilience. The programme was approved in March 2012, began in July 2012 and reached its revised completion date in December 2017. Mangrove activities can protect and rebuild biological carbon stocks, but the project was formally designed for disaster-risk reduction and adaptation. Its official materials do not establish a blue-carbon baseline, additionality assessment, permanence buffer, carbon-credit registry, verified removal volume or issued offsets.
source: Adaptation Fund / United Nations Development Programme / Government of Papua New Guinea
status_note: Approved on 16 March 2012, implemented from 26 July 2012 and officially recorded as completed on 31 December 2017.

subnational_area: Coastal municipalities of Holguín and Las Tunas
document_title: Climate Smart Aquaculture Systems and Resilient Blue Food Industries
notes: This Adaptation Fund concept proposes climate-smart and regenerative aquaculture systems for coastal communities and blue-food industries in eastern Cuba. Planned measures include integrated multi-trophic aquaculture, resilient production and processing infrastructure, circular resource use, ecosystem-based adaptation and maintenance or restoration of supporting coastal ecosystems such as mangroves. The concept refers to oyster, shrimp and sea-cucumber production and seeks to reduce vulnerability to warming, salinization, drought, sea-level rise and extreme weather while supporting food security and inclusive livelihoods. The requested grant is USD 3.9 million for four years. The concept remains under review and does not authorize marine farming sites, define creditable carbon removals, approve a blue-carbon methodology, register units or demonstrate issued credits.
source: Adaptation Fund / United Nations Industrial Development Organization / Cuban partners
status_note: Officially listed in 2026 as a submitted four-year project concept requesting USD 3.9 million; full approval and implementation had not been confirmed.

document_title: Ecosystem-Based Adaptation of the Comoros Coastal Zone
notes: This Adaptation Fund proposal requests approximately USD 9.98 million for ecosystem-based adaptation along the Comoros coast. The project design includes restoration of degraded coastal ecosystems, community-based management, climate-resilient livelihoods, institutional strengthening and monitoring. Proposal materials identify restoration of approximately thirty hectares of mangroves and improved management of associated coastal habitats as concrete measures for reducing erosion, flooding and ecosystem vulnerability. The programme is relevant to coastal blue carbon because mangrove recovery can rebuild biomass and soil-carbon stocks, but its formal objective is adaptation rather than carbon-credit generation. The official project page does not show final approval or implementation status, and the proposal does not establish verified removals, an approved crediting methodology, registry registration or issued carbon units.
source: Adaptation Fund / United Nations Environment Programme / Government of Comoros
status_note: Adaptation Fund proposal materials were published in 2022; the official project page did not display confirmation of final approval, implementation or closure.

subnational_area: Asilulu, Ureng and Lima villages, Central Maluku
document_title: Enhancing the Adaptation Capability of Coastal Communities in Asilulu, Ureng and Lima, Central Maluku
notes: This Adaptation Fund project supports coastal adaptation in three Central Maluku villages through fisheries resilience, coastal-ecosystem repair, alternative livelihoods and infrastructure for flooding and tidal-wave risks. Implementation materials include rehabilitation of coastal habitats and development of floating seaweed cultivation as a livelihood option, while the broader project strengthens local capacity and management of climate-sensitive marine resources. The project was approved in October 2021, began in August 2022 and is still listed by the Fund as under implementation despite an original expected completion date in August 2025. Seaweed cultivation and habitat rehabilitation can contribute to biological carbon pathways, but the project does not provide a crediting baseline, permanence framework, verified removal volume, registry registration or issued credits.
source: Adaptation Fund / Kemitraan / Harmony Alam Indonesia Foundation
status_note: Approved on 21 October 2021, started on 29 August 2022 and officially remains listed as under implementation on the current project page.

document_title: Building Urban Climate Resilience in South-Eastern Africa
notes: This regional Adaptation Fund programme supports participatory urban resilience planning and priority adaptation subprojects in four cities across south-eastern Africa. The Morondava component includes community-based mangrove restoration and nursery development to strengthen coastal protection, while the wider programme covers flood management, resilient infrastructure, governance capacity, knowledge exchange and support for vulnerable urban populations. The programme was approved in July 2019, began in June 2020 and remains officially listed as under implementation after a revised completion date in April 2025. Its mangrove component can conserve and increase biological carbon stocks, but the regional programme is not a blue-carbon credit project. Public materials do not establish additionality, permanence, a carbon registry, verified removals or issued carbon credits.
source: Adaptation Fund / UN-Habitat / National and municipal partners in south-eastern Africa
status_note: Approved on 15 July 2019, started on 23 June 2020 and remains officially listed as under implementation following a revised completion date of 21 April 2025.

subnational_area: Lembar and Sekotong, West Lombok, West Nusa Tenggara
document_title: Village-Based Coastal Adaptation and Resilience in Lombok Province of West Nusa Tenggara
notes: This Adaptation Fund proposal targets coastal villages exposed to tidal flooding, shoreline change and livelihood disruption in West Lombok. Proposed activities include village climate-risk planning, community field schools, early-warning and preparedness measures, livelihood diversification, rehabilitation of coastal ecosystems and mangrove planting across approximately one hundred hectares with community-based nurseries. The official project page lists a requested grant of USD 998,739, a two-year duration and a proposal-submitted status. The project therefore remains under review rather than under implementation. Its mangrove work could restore coastal biological carbon stocks, but the proposal does not establish a project-level carbon baseline, additionality or permanence rules, an approved crediting methodology, registry registration, verified removal outcomes or issued carbon credits.
source: Adaptation Fund / Kemitraan / Indonesian local partners
status_note: Officially listed as a submitted two-year proposal requesting USD 998,739; final approval, financing transfer and implementation start had not been confirmed.

document_title: Safekeeping-Surviving-Sustaining towards Resilience: 3S Approach for Pekalongan City
notes: The Pekalongan 3S programme combines climate-risk assessment, coastal-protection interventions, local adaptation planning, livelihood support, sanitation improvements, institutional coordination and monitoring in a low-lying Indonesian coastal city. Project implementation includes soft and hard shoreline measures and rehabilitation of coastal vegetation, including mangrove-related protection activities, to address tidal flooding, erosion and land subsidence. The Adaptation Fund approved the programme in September 2020, implementation began in July 2021 and the completion date was revised to November 2026. The programme remains officially listed as under implementation. Although ecosystem rehabilitation may protect coastal carbon stocks, the project is not registered as a carbon-removal activity and does not report a blue-carbon baseline, verified removals, methodology approval or issued credits.
source: Adaptation Fund / Kemitraan / Government and communities of Pekalongan City
status_note: Approved on 23 September 2020, started on 15 July 2021 and remains under implementation with a revised completion date of 12 November 2026.

subnational_area: Coastal wetland and mangrove areas of former Trà Vinh and Bến Tre
document_title: Innovative Financial Incentives for Adaptation in Wetland Livelihoods (IFIA) — Implementation Phase
notes: The IFIA project was formally launched in November 2025 to pilot and institutionalize financing mechanisms for climate adaptation in coastal wetland livelihoods. The USD 5 million initiative supports approximately 21,000 vulnerable people engaged in eco-aquaculture, eco-tourism and sustainable use of mangrove and wetland resources. Activities include an adaptation research and innovation fund, tailored financial products, private-sector partnerships, policy learning and mechanisms intended to expand sustainable wetland and mangrove management. The implementation period runs from 2025 to 2029. The project concerns adaptation finance and ecosystem stewardship rather than carbon-credit generation. It does not establish a blue-carbon methodology, determine project additionality or permanence, register offsets, quantify independently verified removals or report issued carbon credits.
source: Government of Viet Nam / International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD)
status_note: Formally launched on 12 November 2025 for implementation during 2025–2029, with a mid-term review planned for 2027 and terminal evaluation in 2029.

document_title: Peraturan Menteri Kelautan dan Perikanan Nomor 1 Tahun 2025 tentang Tata Cara Penyelenggaraan Nilai Ekonomi Karbon Sektor Kelautan
notes: This binding ministerial regulation establishes procedures for implementing carbon economic value instruments in Indonesia's marine sector. It links marine mitigation activities to national climate targets and the wider national carbon economic value system. Its chapters address implementation arrangements, measurement, reporting and verification, official recording, greenhouse-gas emission-reduction certification, management of funds, monitoring and evaluation. The official preparatory materials identify mangroves and seagrass ecosystems as principal blue-carbon assets and contemplate market and non-market mechanisms, including carbon trading, offsets and results-based payments. The regulation creates a governance and compliance framework, but it does not automatically approve individual projects, establish project baselines, verify removals or issue carbon credits without subsequent registration, certification, permitting and regulatory oversight.
source: Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries, Republic of Indonesia
status_note: Enacted on 6 January 2025, promulgated on 14 January 2025 and officially listed as in force.

document_title: Keputusan Menteri Kelautan dan Perikanan Nomor 52 Tahun 2024 tentang Peta Jalan Mitigasi Perubahan Iklim Sektor Kelautan dan Perikanan
notes: This ministerial decision adopts a climate-change mitigation roadmap for Indonesia's marine and fisheries sector. The roadmap provides an official planning basis for sectoral mitigation priorities, institutional coordination, programme sequencing and implementation through marine and fisheries policies. Its blue-carbon dimension includes protection, management and restoration of mangrove and seagrass ecosystems and development of the evidence, monitoring and governance needed to recognize their mitigation contribution. The decision is an internally binding national planning instrument rather than a project-level authorization or carbon-credit methodology. It sets strategic direction and can support later regulations, investment programmes and market instruments, but it does not by itself designate every implementation site, determine additionality and permanence, certify quantified removals, register projects or issue tradable carbon units.
source: Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries, Republic of Indonesia
status_note: Adopted on 28 July 2024 and officially listed by the ministry's legal information system as in force.

document_title: Kajian Teknis Penyusunan Rancangan Peraturan Menteri Kelautan dan Perikanan tentang Penyelenggaraan Nilai Ekonomi Karbon Sektor Kelautan atau Blue Carbon
notes: This technical study supplied the analytical basis for Indonesia's later marine-sector carbon economic value regulation. It identifies the need for complete maps and datasets, a measurement, reporting and verification framework, methodologies for calculating blue-carbon units, market mechanisms, non-market mechanisms and recording through the national climate registry. The study discusses mangrove and seagrass mitigation, risks from seagrass degradation, restoration scenarios, integration of blue carbon into the Nationally Determined Contribution and use of IPCC wetland guidance. It is a preparatory assessment rather than a binding rule and its policy-development function was substantially fulfilled by the 2025 regulation. It does not itself establish legal project eligibility, certify a methodology, authorize restoration, verify removal quantities or issue carbon units.
source: Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries, Republic of Indonesia
status_note: Prepared as a 2023 technical analysis supporting the regulation that was subsequently enacted in January 2025.

document_title: Keputusan Menteri Kelautan dan Perikanan Nomor 82 Tahun 2025 tentang Program Penyusunan Peraturan Menteri dan Keputusan Menteri di Lingkungan Kementerian Kelautan dan Perikanan Tahun 2026
notes: This ministerial decision adopts the Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries' formal regulatory drafting programme for 2026. One scheduled instrument is a 2025–2030 marine and fisheries carbon-trading roadmap covering blue-carbon ecosystems, specifically mangroves and seagrass, carbon trading related to fisheries vessels and aquaculture areas, results-based payments, carbon levies, governance, methodologies and monitoring systems. The decision therefore documents an official commitment to develop a more detailed sectoral carbon-market roadmap and assigns a timetable within the ministry's legal work programme. It is not the roadmap itself and does not establish trading eligibility, issue allowances or credits, approve blue-carbon projects or quantify removals. Its function is regulatory planning and coordination, and completion of the scheduled downstream instrument requires a separate formal decision.
source: Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries, Republic of Indonesia
status_note: Adopted on 16 December 2025 as the ministry's binding legal-drafting programme for calendar year 2026.

document_title: Peraturan Presiden Nomor 110 Tahun 2025 tentang Penyelenggaraan Instrumen Nilai Ekonomi Karbon dan Pengendalian Emisi Gas Rumah Kaca Nasional
notes: This presidential regulation replaces the previous national carbon economic value framework and establishes Indonesia's current system for carbon allocation, Nationally Determined Contribution preparation, carbon economic value instruments, transparency, monitoring, evaluation, supervision and financing. It expressly recognizes blue-carbon management as a mitigation subsector coordinated by the minister responsible for marine affairs and fisheries, while mangrove management remains connected with the forestry subsector. The regulation therefore supplies the national legal architecture within which marine-sector rules, targets, registries, trading and results-based mechanisms operate. It is a binding cross-sector framework rather than a project permit. Individual blue-carbon activities must still comply with sectoral rules, baselines, MRV, safeguards and registration requirements, and the presidential regulation does not itself verify project removals or issue credits.
source: President of the Republic of Indonesia
status_note: Enacted and promulgated on 10 October 2025, officially in force and replacing Presidential Regulation No. 98 of 2021.

document_title: Rancangan Peraturan Menteri Kelautan dan Perikanan tentang Tata Cara Penyelenggaraan Nilai Ekonomi Karbon Sektor Kelautan
notes: This official draft set out the proposed legal design for implementing carbon economic value instruments in Indonesia's marine sector before adoption of the final ministerial regulation. It described eligible marine mitigation activities, including management of mangrove, seagrass and other qualifying blue-carbon ecosystems, domestic and international carbon trading, emissions trading, offsets, direct transactions, buffer requirements, registration in the national climate registry, results-based payments, MRV, certification and monitoring. The draft is retained as a distinct formal rulemaking version because it documents the design considered during legal preparation. It no longer has an independent operational role after enactment of Ministerial Regulation No. 1 of 2025. It did not itself create binding project rights, verify removals or issue carbon credits.
source: Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries, Republic of Indonesia
status_note: Formal 2025 draft superseded by the final ministerial regulation promulgated on 14 January 2025.

subnational_area: Four pilot provinces to be selected during project preparation
document_title: GEF Project 12073 — Enhancing Policy Coherence for a Sustainable Blue Economy in Indonesia
notes: This GEF full-size project concept proposes a unified data, ocean-accounting and decision-support framework for marine and coastal policy in Indonesia. Planned activities include strengthening ocean accounts in four provinces, standardizing methodologies and datasets, improving cross-ministerial and land-sea policy coherence, integrating ecosystem values into spatial and development planning and aligning public and private investment with biodiversity and climate resilience. Project documentation also anticipates better evidence for restoration monitoring, natural-capital valuation and potential blue-finance or blue-carbon investment cases. The concept was approved with a GEF grant and substantial co-financing, but it has not yet reached full implementation approval. It does not independently restore a defined blue-carbon site, establish a crediting methodology, verify removals or issue carbon credits.
source: Global Environment Facility (GEF) / United Nations Environment Programme
status_note: GEF concept approved on 19 December 2025; full project approval and implementation were not shown on the official project page.

document_title: UK Marine Strategy Part One: 2026 Update
notes: This policy update provides the current assessment of the environmental status of United Kingdom seas and establishes objectives, targets and indicators for the next six-year Marine Strategy cycle. It supplies an overarching monitoring and governance framework for protecting, preventing deterioration of and restoring marine ecosystems where practical or necessary. Climate change is treated as a cross-cutting pressure, and the accompanying government response recognizes continued work on marine carbon evidence, coastal habitats and the potential treatment of blue-carbon ecosystems in wider climate and inventory policy. The strategy is not a dedicated carbon-removal programme and does not approve salt-marsh or seagrass projects, quantify additional removals, establish a blue-carbon crediting method or issue credits. Its ONCE role is primarily policy coordination, ecosystem monitoring and evidence development.
source: UK Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs and devolved administrations
status_note: Published on 7 April 2026 as the active Part One framework for the next six-year UK Marine Strategy cycle.

document_title: UK Marine Strategy Part One — Summary of Responses and Government Response
notes: This official consultation outcome records stakeholder evidence and the United Kingdom administrations' response before finalization of the 2026 Marine Strategy Part One update. It discusses climate change as a core pressure on marine environmental status and explains continuing research, assessment and policy development concerning marine carbon, salt marshes, seagrass and greenhouse-gas inventory treatment. The response distinguishes issues included directly in Part One from mitigation and adaptation measures that may be developed through later Marine Strategy stages, national adaptation programmes and devolved blue-carbon initiatives. It is a separate policy-response document rather than the strategy itself. It does not authorize restoration, establish project baselines, certify carbon stocks, create a crediting methodology or demonstrate verified carbon removals, but it documents the government's evidence position and future policy direction.
source: UK Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs and devolved administrations
status_note: Published with the final Marine Strategy update on 7 April 2026 as the official consultation and policy-response record.

document_title: Wilder Humber Multi-Habitat Restoration Programme
notes: Wilder Humber is a five-year, data-led restoration programme operating across the Humber Estuary. It is led by Yorkshire Wildlife Trust and Lincolnshire Wildlife Trust with corporate and public-sector support and combines planting of salt marsh and seagrass, native-oyster reintroduction and reconnection of sand-dune systems. Programme reporting states that eighteen hectares of seagrass had been restored since 2021 and that extensive ecological monitoring is used to measure habitat condition and biodiversity outcomes. Carbon is presented as an emerging future investment pathway because restored habitats can protect sedimentary carbon and compensate for ecosystem carbon loss. The programme is not a carbon-credit methodology or registered offset project and does not report verified removal units or issued credits.
source: Yorkshire Wildlife Trust / Lincolnshire Wildlife Trust and programme partners
status_note: Five-year programme initiated in 2021 and reported as active through its January 2026 European Commission presentation.

subnational_area: Eligible high-nutrient, low-chlorophyll ocean areas within national exclusive economic zones
document_title: Puro Standard Microalgae Carbon Fixation and Sinking Methodology, Edition 2025
notes: This Puro Standard methodology establishes voluntary carbon-removal certification rules for Microalgae Carbon Fixation and Sinking. Eligible activities enhance local microalgae growth on engineered substrates containing bound nutrients and then sink the substrate and attached biomass rapidly into the deep ocean for storage exceeding two hundred years. The methodology specifies site eligibility, scale and deployment limits, environmental impact assessment, baseline data, ecological monitoring, quantification, modeling, uncertainty treatment, third-party verification and safeguards. Puro distinguishes the pathway from uncontrolled ocean fertilization because nutrients remain bound and export is deliberately controlled. Publication creates a crediting pathway but does not authorize marine deployment. Individual projects must secure applicable permits, demonstrate net removal and durability, pass independent audit and satisfy registry requirements before CO2 Removal Certificates can be issued.
source: Puro.earth
status_note: Approved by the Puro.earth Advisory Board on 30 September 2025 and active under the Puro Standard.

document_title: Puro Standard Marine Anoxic Carbon Storage Methodology, Edition 2025
notes: This Puro Standard methodology defines a voluntary certification pathway for Marine Anoxic Carbon Storage. The approach deposits sustainably sourced, lignin-rich terrestrial biomass in deep, oxygen-depleted marine basins where microbial decomposition and animal disturbance are strongly limited, supporting storage for more than two hundred years. The methodology includes site screening, biomass sourcing requirements, baseline and counterfactual assessment, lifecycle greenhouse-gas accounting, durability analysis, monitoring, modeling, field sampling, adaptive management and environmental and social safeguards. It is an active crediting standard but not a dumping permit or deployment authorization. Puro reported that projects remained at the field-trial stage and that no MACS credits had yet been issued; every project must obtain all applicable permits and complete independent audit before CORCs are eligible for issuance.
source: Puro.earth
status_note: Approved by the Puro.earth Advisory Board in April 2025 and active with a conservative durability category exceeding two hundred years.

subnational_area: Permitted coastal or marine storage settings using controlled reactor systems
document_title: Puro Standard Direct Air Capture and Ocean Storage Methodology, Edition 2025 Version 1.1
notes: This Puro Standard methodology provides voluntary certification rules for Direct Air Capture and Ocean Storage. The pathway uses a controlled electrochemical reactor to split seawater into acidic and alkaline streams, exposes the alkaline stream to ambient air so that it absorbs carbon dioxide, re-equilibrates the acidic stream with alkaline rocks and stores carbon as dissolved bicarbonate and solid carbonate. The methodology applies lifecycle accounting, measurement, uncertainty, additionality, durability exceeding one thousand years, environmental impact assessment, water-quality controls, community engagement and third-party verification. It is a private crediting standard rather than a government marine permit. Project-specific intake, discharge, mineral use and storage activities must comply with applicable law, and no credits can be issued without validated net removal, monitoring, independent verification and registry approval.
source: Puro.earth
status_note: Edition 2025 Version 1.1 is listed as an active Puro Standard methodology with a durability category exceeding one thousand years.
